Free device space using Google Photos, with optional automatic cleanup.

1. Enable the BackupDuck service in Android Accessibility settings.
2. Start the 2-minute check.
3. In Google Photos, open your profile, then “Free up space on this device”. Stop before the final Free up button.
4. Return here to see the result.
The read-only check never clicks or deletes. Automatic cleanup requires separate consent and account binding. BackupDuck originals and gallery copies use separate retention rules.

BackupDuck uses Android Accessibility to read selected on-screen controls in Google Photos only during a check you start, for up to 2 minutes. This includes the Free up space message and buttons. Account descriptions, photo labels and screenshots are not collected. Page text is processed in memory on this device; only result categories are kept in memory or included when you export a report. Nothing is sent to a server. No clicks or deletions are performed. You can stop a check here or disable this service in Android Settings.

Connect both devices to the same reachable local network. Tap a pairing option on Receive; BackupDuck starts receiving automatically and opens the code or scanner when ready. On an iPhone, scan the code displayed by this receiver. On a Mac, display a computer pairing code and scan it with this receiver. Camera permission is needed only for scanning. Check the device names after pairing; renaming a device keeps its existing identity and receipts.

The current Android receiver requires Wi-Fi with an IPv4 address. Guest networks, client isolation and some VPN routes can prevent devices from reaching each other even when they show the same network name. Return to the original local network and retry. A Wi-Fi interruption is retried automatically while receiving remains enabled.

The receiver keeps its identity and received files when its Wi-Fi address changes. Updated Apple senders discover the new local address and verify it using the existing pairing before reconnecting. Open the sender to allow discovery; a manually paused backup stays paused. If the network blocks discovery, scan a new pairing code. Keep both apps updated. Do not clear app data to reconnect.

Start receiving before leaving BackupDuck. Android runs the receiver as a foreground service and may show an ongoing notification; allow notifications when requested. If your phone restricts background activity, check its battery settings. Stopping reception explicitly prevents automatic restoration until you start it again.
After a restart or system stop

Settings → Receiving controls restoration after restart. On Android 15 or later, this app asks you to open BackupDuck to resume instead of starting reception at boot. The system can also limit long-running background work. Return to the app and start receiving if prompted; existing receipts and partial transfers are retained.
The sender also needs time to run

A ready receiver cannot force a sender to run. iOS decides when background preparation and requests can continue; uninterrupted locked-screen backup is not guaranteed. Keep the sender open for an initial large import, and reopen it if work stalls. A Mac sender needs the app running and the computer awake.

BackupDuck confirms receipt only after all resources for an item arrive and pass integrity checks. A motion photo can contain an original still image and a paired video under one logical item. A processing failure after receipt does not require uploading those originals again.
Published means a device-gallery copy exists

The receiver prepares a system-gallery copy after receipt, including supported Motion Photo conversion and burst metadata. Check Transfers for processing status and retry failed processing there. Grouped burst display in an external gallery depends on that gallery; source originals and per-frame receipts remain separate.
Cloud backup is a separate operation

Google Photos handles its own upload. Select the intended account and enable backup for the BackupDuck device folder if needed. Receiving or gallery publication does not confirm cloud backup. The automatic space experiment only removes device copies Google Photos confirms are backed up; the page check is for troubleshooting and does not free space.

Storage limits includes an original-storage budget and a minimum free-space reserve. Gallery copies and conversion scratch files also occupy the phone. Increasing the original budget does not create free disk space. If space is insufficient, review the separate original and gallery totals before choosing what to retain.

New installations reclaim app relay originals after their system-gallery copy has passed verification. Existing retention preferences stay unchanged. Failed, pending or in-use originals are kept. This does not delete gallery copies or confirm cloud upload. You can also export a verified original archive before explicitly reclaiming eligible files; an archive stored on this phone still uses space.

When you explicitly enable relay mode in Storage, BackupDuck verifies the completed gallery copy before reclaiming eligible staging originals. Missing, changed or unverified copies keep their originals. A converted motion copy is not a byte-for-byte archive of its original image/video pair. Turning relay off stops new reclamation; it cannot restore already reclaimed originals. This policy does not verify cloud backup.

For a sender upload failure, inspect the sender queue and its retry controls. If originals are already received but gallery processing failed, filter Transfers for failed processing and use Retry failed processing. Space-related processing waits are checked again automatically while receiving is active. Repeated re-imports are not a substitute for resolving the underlying error.

Open Settings → Diagnostics → Export logs. Include the time of the issue and whether the sender or receiver was in the foreground. Reports contain bounded event records such as stages, task identifiers and byte counts; they do not include photo content or pairing credentials. Review a report before sharing it. The experimental screen check has its own Export check result action.

Use App updates in Settings to check for and install a new officially signed version. If Android reports an incompatible signature, this installation came from a different source. Do not uninstall or clear storage; that can remove private originals.

Automatically check below %1$s available. New transfers pause during cleanup and resume according to the storage reserve. Password-protected screens need manual unlocking.

BackupDuck uses Android Accessibility to navigate Google Photos and press Free up space only when its official message confirms these items are safely backed up. This may include backed-up device photos from other apps, not only BackupDuck. It never presses Delete or empties cloud trash. The selected account is read in memory and only its fingerprint is saved locally. No account text, screenshots or photo labels are stored or sent. Cleanup is off by default; bind an account, then enable automation or start one cleanup. Each run is limited to 5 minutes. You can stop here or disable the accessibility service in Android Settings. An uncertain cleanup is checked without pressing Free up again. During cleanup, BackupDuck may wake the screen and dismiss a lock screen without a PIN, password or pattern. Secure lock screens require manual unlocking.
